lesson.label: Connectivity vs. spatial arrangement
lesson.title: Connectivity vs. spatial arrangement
lesson.tag: Same formula is only the first test

cards.rule: Constitutional isomers share a molecular formula but differ in connectivity. Stereoisomers have the same connectivity and differ in spatial arrangement. Conformers interconvert by rotations about single bonds.
cards.cue: Formula → connections → space. Compare in that order.
cards.trap: A different drawing orientation does not prove isomerism. Rotating the whole molecule changes neither connectivity nor configuration.
cards.app: An alcohol and an ether can share a formula but differ in hydrogen-bond donation, boiling point, and reactivity.

steps.label: 1. Alcohol connectivity
steps.text: Count two carbons, six hydrogens, and one oxygen. The oxygen bears H and can donate a hydrogen bond.

steps.label: 2. Ether connectivity
steps.text: The same formula now has oxygen between two carbons. No O–H bond is present. This is a constitutional isomer, not a different conformation.

steps.label: 3. Branched framework
steps.text: Butane and 2-methylpropane are another constitutional-isomer pair: identical formula, different carbon skeletons.

cards.rule: In butane, anti and gauche are staggered conformations; eclipsed conformations have greater torsional strain. Cyclohexane chairs reduce angle and torsional strain. A ring flip exchanges axial and equatorial positions while retaining up/down orientation.
cards.cue: Anti = 180° between the methyl groups. Gauche = 60°. In a chair, bulky groups usually prefer equatorial sites.
cards.trap: Axial is not synonymous with up: axial directions alternate around the ring. A chair flip preserves cis/trans relationships.
cards.app: Conformational preferences affect how a flexible drug fits a binding site; a more populated conformer need not be the bound conformer.

steps.label: 1. Rotate a single bond
steps.text: Look down the middle C–C bond of butane. Adjust the angle to compare torsional and methyl–methyl interactions.

diagram.caption: Butane viewed along C2–C3: blue front bonds and green rear bonds.

steps.label: 2. Ring constraints
steps.text: This hexagon shows connectivity only, not a flat equilibrium geometry. Cyclohexane normally adopts a chair. An axial substituent interacts with axial groups at C3 and C5; an equatorial position avoids much of this crowding.

lesson.label: Chirality, enantiomers, and meso compounds
lesson.title: Chirality, enantiomers, and meso compounds
lesson.tag: Mirror image ≠ always a different molecule

cards.rule: A tetrahedral carbon with four different substituents is a common stereogenic center. Enantiomers are nonsuperimposable mirror images. Diastereomers are stereoisomers that are not mirror images; E/Z pairs qualify too.
cards.cue: One inverted center in a one-center molecule gives its enantiomer. With several centers, compare the entire molecule.
cards.trap: 2ⁿ is a maximum number of stereoisomers, not a guarantee. Internal symmetry can make a molecule with stereocenters achiral (meso). R/S does not predict the sign of optical rotation.
cards.app: Enantiomers have equal properties in achiral environments except opposite optical rotations; chiral receptors can distinguish them.

steps.label: 1. Identify four groups
steps.text: The alcohol-bearing carbon is bonded to OH, H, methyl, and ethyl: four different groups. The flat connectivity drawing alone does not assign R or S.

challenge.explanation: Atom B has four different substituents.

steps.label: 2. Count with symmetry
steps.text: Butane-2,3-diol has two potential stereocenters. Its (2R,3S) and (2S,3R) descriptions refer to the same meso compound because of symmetry; the RR and SS forms are an enantiomeric pair. Total: three stereoisomers.

cards.rule: Rank directly attached atoms by atomic number; isotopes by mass. Resolve ties one sphere at a time using sorted atom lists. Treat multiple bonds with duplicate-atom bookkeeping. With priority 4 away, clockwise 1→2→3 is R and counterclockwise is S.
cards.cue: Fischer: horizontal comes forward; vertical goes back. If group 4 is horizontal, reverse the apparent result.
cards.trap: A 180° in-plane Fischer rotation preserves configuration; a 90° rotation does not. D/L is a relative-configuration convention, not a synonym for R/S or +/−.
cards.app: Most proteinogenic L amino acids are S; L cysteine is R because sulfur changes CIP ranking. Glycine has no stereogenic alpha carbon.

steps.label: 1. Rank the substituents
steps.text: OH ranks first because O outranks C. Ethyl outranks methyl by the next sphere: [C,H,H] beats [H,H,H]. H is fourth.

diagram.caption: Fischer projection of butan-2-ol. Horizontal bonds point toward you; vertical bonds point away.

steps.label: 2. Orient then assign
steps.text: In this Fischer projection, 1→2→3 appears clockwise, but H is horizontal and points toward you. Reverse the apparent sense: the projection is S.

diagram.caption: Fischer projection of butan-2-ol. Horizontal bonds point toward you; vertical bonds point away.

steps.label: 3. Mirror the projection
steps.text: Interchanging H and OH inverts this single center. The mirrored projection is R and represents the enantiomer.

diagram.caption: Mirror Fischer projection: exchange the two horizontal groups.

cards.rule: E/Z is defined only when each double-bond carbon has two different substituents. Rank each end by CIP: Z places the higher-priority groups on the same side; E on opposite sides. A racemate has equal amounts of two enantiomers and zero net rotation under ordinary conditions.
cards.cue: Z: together. E: opposite. Enantiomeric excess is the absolute difference in enantiomer percentages.
cards.trap: Cis/trans cannot replace E/Z in every alkene. Zero optical rotation can mean a racemate or an achiral compound; it does not identify which.
cards.app: If a pure enantiomer rotates +20° under the same conditions, a 75:25 mixture of it and its enantiomer gives +10° (50% ee).

steps.label: 1. Compare the two ends
steps.text: Each alkene carbon bears methyl and H. Methyl outranks H, and the methyl groups lie on opposite sides: E.

steps.label: 2. Same side
steps.text: Both higher-priority methyl groups now lie on the same side: Z. Rotation about C=C would disrupt pi overlap, so these are configurational isomers.
